title: Refs are files. HEAD is a file that names another file.
summary: Open .git and read the branch, the tag and HEAD directly. Then move a branch by editing a ref, and understand packed-refs — the reason your branch file sometimes is not there.
concepts: detached HEAD as a raw sha
mental_model: A ref is a file containing a sha. HEAD is a file containing `ref: refs/heads/main` — a pointer to a pointer. Detaching HEAD means putting a raw sha in that file instead. Everything about branching follows from this.

steps.title: Look at the ref files
steps.why: Branches and tags are files under `.git/refs`, each containing one sha and a newline. There is no database, no index of branches — this is the whole storage layer for refs.
steps.expect: The file's content and `git rev-parse` agree exactly.

verify.label: the branch file contains the commit sha

steps.title: Read HEAD
steps.why: HEAD does not contain a sha — it contains the NAME of a ref. That indirection is exactly what 'being on a branch' means, and why committing moves the branch rather than HEAD itself.
steps.expect: ref: refs/heads/main — a pointer to a pointer.

steps.title: Detach it and look again
steps.why: Checking out a commit writes a raw sha into HEAD instead of a ref name. That is the entire difference between attached and detached — one line in one file.
steps.expect: A bare sha while detached, and the ref line again afterwards.

verify.label: HEAD is attached to main again

steps.title: Move a branch by writing to its ref
steps.why: `update-ref` is the supported way to write a ref, and it records a reflog entry. It is exactly what commit, merge, reset and rebase all call at the end of their work.
steps.expect: The branch jumps to main's commit, with a reflog entry recording it.

verify.cmd: sh -c 'test "$(git rev-parse feature/experiment)" = "$(git rev-parse main)" && echo moved'
verify.label: the branch was moved by writing its ref

steps.title: Create a branch with no branch command
steps.why: Writing a new ref file creates a branch. `git branch` is a convenience around this, plus a couple of safety checks — nothing more.

verify.label: a branch created by writing a ref

steps.title: Pack the refs and watch the files vanish
steps.why: `pack-refs` moves refs into a single `.git/packed-refs` file for speed. This is why `cat .git/refs/heads/main` sometimes says no such file — the ref is real, it is just stored elsewhere.
steps.expect: No loose ref files, one packed-refs file, and every command still working perfectly.

steps.title: Use the command that reads both places
steps.why: `show-ref` and `for-each-ref` consult loose refs and packed-refs together. Any script that reads `.git/refs` directly is broken the moment someone runs gc — this is the practical reason plumbing exists.

verify.label: update-ref -d deletes a ref wherever it is stored
show-ref reads loose and packed refs together
HEAD is an attached symbolic ref

verify.cmd: sh -c 'test "$(git rev-parse feature/experiment)" = "$(git rev-parse main)" && echo moved'
verify.label: you moved a branch by writing its ref directly
refs were packed into packed-refs and still resolve
the hand-made branch was deleted with update-ref -d
every ref points at a real object

pitfalls: Never read `.git/refs/...` in a script. After `git gc` or `git pack-refs` the file is gone and the ref lives in packed-refs — use `git rev-parse` or `git show-ref`.
Writing a ref file by hand with `echo` skips the reflog entry, so your safety net for that move does not exist. Use `git update-ref`.
A branch name with a slash is a directory on disk: `refs/heads/feature/x`. That is why you cannot have both a branch `feature` and a branch `feature/x`.
`git update-ref -d` is the only correct way to delete a ref — deleting the file misses the packed-refs copy and the ref reappears.
cheatsheet: ref: refs/heads/<branch>, or a raw sha when detached
resolve any ref to a sha
read refs wherever they are stored
